title: Portal hypertension in cirrhosis
official: Effects of Metformin on hepatic venous pressure gradient in patients with cirrhosis and portal hypertension – A randomized placebo-controlled study
summary:
Main objective: To evaluate the effect of metformin versus placebo during 28 days on HVPG, in patients with cirrhosis and a HVPG ≥ 12 mm Hg already treated with carvedilol. 
Objectif of the ancillary study : To study the effect of metformin on postprandial changes in systemic haemodynamics and HVPG.
conditions: Portal hypertension (PHT) and consequences in complications of cirrhosis
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. -	Age ≥ 18 years
2. -	Absence of hepatocellular carcinoma outside at least one nodule > 3 cm in diameter, or more than 3 nodules, on ultrasound, CT-scan or MRI performed during the previous 6 months
3. -	Written informed consent to participate in the study
4. -	Medical insurance coverage
5. -	For child-bearing aged women, contraception using oestroprogestative, progestative, intrauterine device, or mechanical contraception
6. -	Diagnosis of cirrhosis based on a liver biopsy, or on clinical, biological, endoscopic, and radiological evidence
7. -	Active cause of cirrhosis, or resolution (alcohol cessation, sustained virological response to direct-acting antiviral treatment for HCV, initiation of nucleoside/nucleotide analog treatment for HBV) for at least 6 months
8. -	Child-Pugh A or B
9. -	High likelihood of HVPG ≥ 12 mm Hg based on investigator’s judgement, _confer criteria in the protocole
10. -	Treatment with carvedilol (≥ 6,25 mg/day) at a stable dose for at least one month
Exclusion criteria:
1. -	Serum total bilirubin > 50 µmol/L
2. -	Prothrombin ratio < 50 %
3. -	Transaminases > 5 ULN
4. -	Need for at least one paracentesis for ascites fluid evacuation in the last 6 months
